decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line builds directly on the firm's core design, ergonomics and fixing know-how, and such lines typically sell for many years, so the lack of website mentions in 2020 and 2021 more likely reflects normal catalogue status than failure.
This multi-model handle family fits the firm's certified systems and established competencies, which makes it cheap to maintain and refine within long architectural hardware lifecycles.

This single design lies close to the core offer and costs little to keep listed, but its narrower scope and absence from the website make a range clean-up somewhat more plausible than for the handle families.
Like C, this design draws on the firm's ergonomic expertise, but as a single design that has not been mentioned since launch it is a candidate for rationalisation, though not yet a clear one.
A lever handle family with several models adds system breadth and rests on knowledge the firm already holds, so continuing it remains the natural choice.

The electronic access flagship matches the strategic move toward digital building organisation, and in-house R&D lets the firm absorb market feedback and upgrade the system, although fast digital product cycles raise some risk that a newer generation replaces it.
